svg.title: gov-tla B6 — SenateRules.tla: the filibuster — cloture at three-fifths, the reconciliation clock and the nuclear option — and why a bare majority need not prevail
svg.desc: Not constitutional text: the Senate's own rules under Art. I §5 cl. 2, layered on simple-majority passage, as of 1975 (README § SenateRules.tla). Each measure moves from debate to a vote; debate closes by cloture at three-fifths or, for a reconciliation bill, by the statutory clock; the threshold falls only by amending the rule on two-thirds or by a majority's precedent (the nuclear option). TLC checks 51 rows, every one as expected, and TLAPS proves the five safety properties for a Senate of any size in 201 obligations. The filibuster is drawn as the failure of a leads-to: MajorityPrevails is a COUNTEREXAMPLE under FairSpec and holds under NuclearSpec; it and the other temporal rows are checked, not proved. This models the rules' procedure: it is an exercise, not law (README, opening).

Each measure moves from debate to a vote; debate closes by cloture at three-fifths or, for a reconciliation bill, by the statutory clock; the threshold falls only by amending the rule on two-thirds or by a majority's precedent (the nuclear option). TLC checks 51 rows, every one as expected, and TLAPS proves the

five safety properties for a Senate of any size in 201 obligations. The filibuster is drawn as the failure of a leads-to: MajorityPrevails is a COUNTEREXAMPLE under FairSpec and holds under NuclearSpec; it and the other temporal rows are checked, not proved. This models the rules' procedure: it is an exercise, not law (README, opening).

svg.text: Checked means TLC explored every reachable state at the constants in the row list. Proved means TLAPS discharged every obligation for every value of the constants the module's named assumptions admit. Sampled means random simulation found no error, and is never cited as a check; this module has no sampled row. "None of these is a claim about law or practice" (README § How the specs are written and checked).

text.tspan: Votes at the rows' constants (the diagram's arithmetic from the operators)

svg.text: Majority(n) == 2 * n > N; ThreeFifths(n) == 5 * n >= 3 * N ("of the Senators duly chosen and sworn"); TwoThirdsOf(n,
p) == 3 * n >= 2 * p ("of those present and voting"), with a quorum, Majority(present), present.
N = 7 (the rows' default)
N = 5 (rows c5-safety, pq5-*)
README: "With seven Senators, a majority (four) is short of three-fifths (five). With five, the two are the same, and the rows show that
M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION then removes nothing." TwoThirdsOf(n, 4): four present, the least quorum of seven; AmendRule needs
ayes <= present.

text.tspan: The five safety properties (header PROPERTIES), each with what can break it

svg.text: Header: Rule XXII: "debate on a measure is
closed by cloture only when the votes meet
the threshold then in force for its kind (flag
shortCloture)."
Set only by step 2, never cleared.
Header: Rule XXII; Budget Act s.310(e):
"debate on a measure ends without cloture
only if it is a reconciliation bill (flag
debateCut)."
Set only by step 3, never cleared.
Header: Art. I s.5, s.7, as Constitution.tla
reads them: "no measure passes without a
majority of the Senate; the rules raise the bar
and never lower it (flag minorityPassage)."
Set only by step 4, never cleared.
Header: Rule XXII cl.2; Rule V cl.2 (1959):
"the cloture rule is amended, as a rule, only
on two-thirds of those present and voting, a
quorum present (flag shortRulesChange)."
Set only by step 7, never cleared.
Header: "the filibuster itself: no measure
other than a reconciliation bill is past debate
(Closed, Passed or Rejected) while
three-fifths cloture governs its kind unless
three-fifths support it. Not a flag: it holds
because the threshold only falls, so if it is
three-fifths now it was three-fifths when
debate closed."
A state predicate. Proof module header, in
effect: a measure leaves Debate only by step
2 or 3, and steps 6 and 7 only lower a
threshold.

text.tspan: Key to the numbered steps: each step's guard, the flag it raises, and the mutation that removes its check (
, the actions and the checks each mutation removes)

svg.text: "A measure is taken up, with the support it will have throughout"
(comment).
Guard: stage[m] = "Pending"; any n in Counts = 0..N.
Abstracted: "the motion to proceed and its own cloture (Proceed is
one unconditional step)".
Rule XXII: cloture by three-fifths (README rule table).
Guard: in Debate, not in Reconciliations, ClotureCarries(m):
Meets(cloture[Kind(m)], support[m]).
Raises shortCloture if the votes are short of the threshold in force.
M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION: Majority(support[m]) carries
cloture.
Budget Act of 1974 §310(e): reconciliation debate limited by statute.
Guard: in Debate, TimeLimited(m): m \in Reconciliations.
Raises debateCut if m is not a reconciliation bill.
M_TIME_LIMIT: every measure's debate runs out.
Passage (or confirmation) by a majority.
Guard: Closed, PassCarries(m): Majority(support[m]).
Raises minorityPassage if m lacks a majority.
M_NO_MAJORITY: a closed measure passes on any count.
Guard: Closed, ~Majority(support[m]).
Raises no flag; no mutation touches it.
Precedents of 2013 and 2017: "a point of order … the chair rules
against it, and the majority that supports m overturns the ruling. A
precedent, not a rule" (comment).
Guard: in Debate, not reconciliation, cloture[Kind(m)] =
"ThreeFifths", Majority(support[m]).
Both precedents "are both the one step Nuclear(m) for a nomination;
the module does not split them" (header). No mutation touches it.
Rule XXII cl. 2, Rule V cl. 2: two-thirds present and voting.
Guard: cloture[k] = "ThreeFifths", Majority(present),
ayes <= present, RulesCarry: TwoThirdsOf(ayes, present).
Raises shortRulesChange if short of two-thirds.
M_CONSTITUTIONAL_OPTION: Majority(ayes) carries it.

"Not constitutional text: the Senate's own rules under Art. I §5 cl. 2, layered on the simple-majority passage that Constitution.tla models in PassChamber. The module stands alone and does not extend Constitution.tla. The initial state is
the rules as of 1975."

SenateRules.cfg, for ad hoc runs: SPECIFICATION Spec, seven Senators, one bill, one nomination, one reconciliation bill, INVARIANTS TypeOK Safety; "The checked results come from rows/SenateRules-rows.txt".
"who the Senators are (a measure's support is a count, fixed when it is taken up), the motion to proceed, the thirty hours after cloture, amendments, holds, unanimous
consent, the "talking" filibuster, vacancies, the Vice President's casting vote, the Byrd rule, and raising the threshold again."
"who the Senators are (votes are counts, and a measure's support is fixed when it is taken up, so every vote on it is the same count: no Senator changes sides); the
motion to proceed and its own cloture (Proceed is one unconditional step); the thirty hours after cloture, amendments, holds, unanimous consent and the "talking"
filibuster (debate either goes on or is closed); vacancies (three-fifths is of the whole Senate); the Vice President's casting vote (no row has an even Senate); the Byrd
rule and what may be reconciled; cloture on a reconciliation bill (never needed, not modelled); raising the threshold again (it only falls); the House."

text.tspan: The two lists compared (the diagram's comparison)

svg.text: The header names four things the README's list does not: the motion to proceed's "own cloture", "what may be reconciled", "cloture on a reconciliation bill (never
needed, not modelled)" and "the House".
Everything the README lists the header lists too. Neither list contradicts the other.

text.tspan: The README's mutation table, every row and column, beside the module header and the verdicts read from
README, header and results (the diagram's check)

g.text: "a majority closes debate, as the House does by the previous question. The Senate's rules of 1789 had a previous-question motion, dropped in
1806; whether it ever served to close debate is doubted. Breaks ClotureThreshold and ClosedOnThreeFifths. Binds only where a majority is less
the limit applies to reconciliation only
"every measure is under a statutory debate limit, as reconciliation is. No earlier law. Breaks DebateEndsByCloture and ClosedOnThreeFifths."
"a closed measure passes without a majority. No earlier law. Breaks MajorityFloor."
"Rule XXII amended by a majority: the "constitutional option", that a new Senate may adopt its rules by majority, argued in 1917, 1953, 1957 (Vice
President Nixon's advisory opinion) and 1975, and never adopted; Rule V cl.2 (1959) says the rules continue. Breaks RulesByTwoThirds."

svg.text: README § SenateRules.tla: "With seven Senators, a majority (four) is short of three-fifths (five). With five, the two are the same, and the rows show that M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION then removes nothing." The rows header expects it: "With five Senators, where a majority is three-fifths, M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION HOLDS on ClotureThreshold and ClosedOnThreeFifths" (rows/SenateRules-rows.txt).

text.tspan: The filibuster as the failure of a leads-to: the temporal rows
Checked, not proved · checked by TLC at seven Senators
The module header, LIVENESS, on this row
Status (README § What is not proved; proof module NOT PROVED)

g.text: "a bill with a majority short of three-fifths is debated forever. That is the filibuster"
"a majority facing a filibuster eventually goes nuclear: the filibuster delays only a majority that declines to end it"
"NoBehaviour is violated under each fair spec, so each has a behaviour"

text.tspan: The properties and the fair specs (

svg.text: ReconciliationPrevails: the same over Reconciliations.
FloorVotes: weak fairness on InvokeCloture(m) and Pass(m), "The floor's obligation: a vote that would carry is taken."
ClockRuns: weak fairness on DebateExpires(m), "The statute's: limited debate runs out."
MajorityGoesNuclear: weak fairness on Nuclear(m), "Not an obligation of anyone: the majority's choice to end a filibuster."
FairSpec == Spec /\ FloorVotes /\ ClockRuns; SpecNoClock == Spec /\ FloorVotes; NuclearSpec == FairSpec
/\ MajorityGoesNuclear.
NoBehaviour == <>(shortCloture /\ ~shortCloture): violated, so each fair spec has a behaviour.
"MajorityPrevails: a measure a majority supports, once taken up, passes. Under FairSpec (the floor votes whenever a vote
would carry, and the reconciliation clock runs) it is VIOLATED: a bill with a majority short of three-fifths is debated forever. That
is the filibuster, stated as the failure of a leads-to. It HOLDS under M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION and M_TIME_LIMIT, and under
NuclearSpec, which adds that a majority facing a filibuster eventually goes nuclear: the filibuster delays only a majority that
declines to end it. ReconciliationPrevails HOLDS under FairSpec and fails without the clock (SpecNoClock). NoBehaviour is
violated under each fair spec, so each has a behaviour."
The filibuster is the failure of a leads-to. MajorityPrevails says a measure a majority supports, once taken up, passes.
Under FairSpec, where the floor takes every vote that would carry and the reconciliation clock runs, TLC finds it violated: a bill
with four of seven votes is debated forever. It holds under M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION, under M_TIME_LIMIT, and for reconciliation
bills.
It binds only a majority that declines to end it. MajorityPrevails holds under NuclearSpec, which adds weak fairness on
Nuclear. The witness NeverLawOnMajority is violated: a bill passes on a bare majority once a majority has lowered the
threshold. NeverNominationsOnly is violated too, so the rules since 2013 (majority for nominations, three-fifths for legislation)
are reachable.

text.tspan: Why each verdict (the diagram's reading of the operators, at seven Senators)

svg.text: FairSpec, unmutated: at 4 of 7, step 2 is never enabled (ThreeFifths needs 5), step 3 is not for a bill, and step 6 is enabled
but has no fairness. Weak fairness forces nothing, so debate can go on forever: COUNTEREXAMPLE.
M_PREVIOUS_QUESTION or M_TIME_LIMIT: step 2 or 3 stays enabled for a backed measure, fairness takes it, then step 4:
HOLDS.
NuclearSpec: step 6 is taken, the threshold falls to a majority, then steps 2 and 4: HOLDS.
SpecNoClock: nothing forces step 3 for a reconciliation bill: COUNTEREXAMPLE.

text.tspan: Mutations with a COUNTEREXAMPLE on it, 7 Senators (read)
Inductive strengthening (proof module header, in prose)

g.text: Under every mutation; cited by every lemma that reads a function after an EXCEPT.
A flag set by InvokeCloture; inductive with TypeOK alone (NextClotureThreshold).
A flag set by DebateExpires; inductive with TypeOK alone (NextDebateEndsByCloture).
A flag set by Pass; inductive with TypeOK alone (NextMajorityFloor).
A flag set by AmendRule; inductive with TypeOK alone (NextRulesByTwoThirds).
Inductive with TypeOK as stated (InvC, NextInvC): a measure leaves Debate only by InvokeCloture or DebateExpires, and "a threshold only falls" (ThresholdOnlyFalls).

text.tspan: each of the 4 mutations breaks a conjunct

g.text: By the five theorems above, and PTL.

svg.text: NNat, KindType, InitTypeOK, NextTypeOK, NextCases, NextClotureThreshold, NextDebateEndsByCloture,
NextMajorityFloor, NextRulesByTwoThirds, ThresholdOnlyFalls, NextInvC, MutPreviousQuestionAdmits,
MutTimeLimitAdmits, MutNoMajorityAdmits, MutConstitutionalOptionAdmits
One lemma per mutation, Mut…Admits, says what it lets through; "the counterexamples themselves are TLC's" (proof module).
"The base module's named ASSUME FiniteSenate, and only for TypeOK (the count 0 is a count of the Senate). MutOK and
KindsDisjoint are not used. So the theorems hold for a Senate of any size and any number of bills, nominations and
reconciliation bills."
README: "The proof (SenateRules_proof.tla) proves each safety property for a Senate of any size, assuming only the
mutations that break it. Four properties are flags. ClosedOnThreeFifths is inductive with TypeOK as stated, because a
measure leaves debate only by cloture or, if it is a reconciliation bill, by the clock, and a threshold only falls (
ThresholdOnlyFalls). The two leads-to properties are checked, not proved."

text.tspan: The prover and what was proved (read)

svg.text: 201 obligations, all proved, 2026.11.19.
Prover: tlapm 1.6.0-pre commit ff40755 (x86_64-linux-gnu); backends: Z3 4.8.9; Zenon 0.8.4 [a268]; Isabelle2025; LS4.
Modules by sha256: SenateRules.tla, SenateRules_proof.tla, each equal to the tree now (checked at build time).
Names SenateRules-results-2026.11.19b.txt by its sha256, also equal now.

text.tspan: Not proved (proof module header, NOT PROVED)

svg.text: MajorityPrevails and ReconciliationPrevails: "each is a leads-to quantified over measures, and the pinned prover has
no sound route for a quantified leads-to". Checked by TLC, with NoBehaviour.
"Reachability (the Never... witnesses) and the mutations' counterexamples: existential, so TLC's."

text.tspan: The constants, and the two TLC results files dated 2026.11.19

svg.text: "seven Senators, the fewest odd number at which a majority (four) is short of three-fifths (five); one bill, one nomination and one reconciliation bill."
Results file Constants: Senators = {s1, s2, s3, s4, s5, s6, s7}; Legislation = {law}; Nominations = {nom}; Reconciliations = {rec}.
Three rows override Senators with five (c5-safety, pq5-cloture, pq5-threefifths).

text.tspan: What differs between the two files (read at build time)

svg.text: SenateRules-results-2026.11.19.txt and SenateRules-results-2026.11.19b.txt differ on lines 1, 4, 5 only: the title, and the Modules: and Rows: digests.
The earlier title ends "; a sketch, unproved"; the named file's does not.
Every row, verdict and state count is the same.
The earlier file's SenateRules.tla and row-list digests are not those of the files in the tree now; the named file's are.
scripts/tlc_rows.py "never overwrites" a results file. "A rerun that reproduces a file says so; one that differs is written beside it with a letter suffix."
corpus.RESULTS names SenateRules-results-2026.11.19b.txt, and this diagram draws from it alone.
